newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks end lower, pessimism looms.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks end lower, pessimism looms.

text.p: Singapore stocks dipped on Thursday as investors largely stayed on the sidelines in fear of further drops, dealers said.
The Straits Times Industrial Index (STII) ended 2.81 points down at 1,990.68 after hitting a low of 1,982.48, dampened by a fall in Fraser & Neave, which shed S$0.10 to end at S$10.40.
Dealers said the expectation of poor F&N results due on Friday added to the gloom and they predicted further selling of the stock. Total market turnover was just 109 million.
They said there was some accumulation of second-liner stocks, including retail company Metro Holdings.
Metro rose S$0.18 to S$4.60. Newly-listed Huan Hsin was active with over 4.8 million shares changing hands.

Speculation that health group Raffles Medical could be a potential merger or takeover target for a larger medical group spurred trading in the stock, dealers said. It hit a new high of S$0.765 before ending at S$0.735, up two cents with over 3.6 million shares traded.
"Talks of its potential takeover or merger surfaced after speculation on Parkway Holdings," said a dealer. Healthcare group Parkway is seen a potential takeover target of DBS Land.
